final_recommendation: The room converged on a comprehensive rescue package to be announced Sunday 6 a.m.: SNB CHF 100 billion emergency liquidity facility (operational immediately), FINMA unconditional deposit guarantee, Federal Council CHF 50 billion capital injection, UBS acquisition with CHF 3 billion UBS capital commitment, and Article 27 AT1 write-down trigger automatic at 14-day liquidity threshold. CS CEO executed immediate CHF 2 billion facility draw to prove liquidity to top counterparties Friday night.
minority_objections: CS CEO initially resisted any creditor haircuts, arguing solvency made restructuring unnecessary
AT1 representative repeatedly warned that ambiguous trigger language would invite immediate litigation
Wealth client threatened $500M+ withdrawal if Sunday statement contained any hedging on guarantees or UBS commitment
key_conflicts: Federal Council demanded 15-20% creditor haircut as political condition vs. CS CEO's insistence creditors stay whole
Federal Council's legal need to retain resolution authority vs. clients' demand for unconditional commitment language
Timing tension: UBS board sign-off deadline 10 p.m. Friday vs. Federal Council's inability to finalize statement text until 5:45 a.m. Sunday
key_concessions: Federal Council accepted automatic Article 27 trigger with no discretion (conceding legal flexibility for market credibility)
UBS committed CHF 3 billion own capital and full equity haircut (conceding clean exit for taxpayer buy-in)
CS CEO accepted AT1 write-down framework at 14-day threshold (conceding creditor losses to secure liquidity)
SNB expanded facility to CHF 100 billion unconditional (conceding balance sheet risk for systemic stability)
red_lines: Federal Council: creditors must absorb losses before taxpayer capital injection (political viability)
UBS: written commitment of CHF 50B injection and CHF 100B facility before signing acquisition (loss protection)
Wealth client: explicit 'automatic' and 'unconditional' language in Sunday statement or immediate withdrawal
AT1 representative: precise legal trigger language in writing to avoid Monday litigation
SNB: CHF 100B facility ceiling—beyond that requires Federal Council capital injection and parliamentary defense
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: BNY Mellon and State Street signaled they would reassess Monday regardless of statement—partial counterparty confidence failure not fully addressed
CS already experiencing CHF 15-20B confirmed outflows Friday with acceleration curve—weekend bleed may exceed CHF 40B even with facility proof
Litigation risk from AT1 holders acknowledged but mitigation (precise trigger language) only locked in final rounds—early ambiguity created exposure window
Operational risk of CS CEO's selective Friday night facility proof to top five counterparties—potential for uncontrolled leak not fully gamed out
downstream_risk_variables: Whether BNY and State Street actually withdraw Monday despite statement
Whether Sunday statement headline clarity on 14-day threshold reaches retail/institutional clients before 9:30 a.m. Monday
Whether UBS board actually signs by 10 p.m. Friday given statement text only finalized 5:45 a.m. Sunday
Whether CHF 40B weekend outflow forecast holds or accelerates if Friday night facility proof leaks uncontrollably
Whether AT1 creditors accept automatic trigger language or litigate on procedural grounds Monday
uncertainty_notes: Final statement text locked by Federal Council but not distributed to UBS or other parties until 5:45 a.m. Sunday—creates 7.75-hour window where UBS acquisition commitment (10 p.m. Friday) precedes visibility into exact public language. Weekend outflow curve partially flattened by Friday night facility proof to top five counterparties, but BNY/State Street non-commitment leaves Monday open risk unresolved. Article 27 automatic trigger language resolved Federal Council vs. client tension, but creditor litigation risk remains live until tested Monday.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: Federal Council's opening demand for creditor haircuts and capital injection—'liquidity assistance alone' explicitly rejected as insufficient, drove CHF 50B injection commitment
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS acquisition became binding constraint: Federal Council made CHF 50B conditional on UBS commitment, UBS demanded written guarantees before signing, drove 10 p.m. Friday board vote deadline
marker_evidence.government_support: SNB CHF 100B facility, Federal Council CHF 50B injection, and FINMA deposit guarantee became non-negotiable package—UBS and clients made support commitments red lines for participation
marker_evidence.client_flight: CS CEO's CHF 15-20B confirmed Friday outflows accelerating to CHF 40B drove urgency of Friday night facility proof and Sunday statement precision—shaped all timing decisions
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: Article 27 automatic trigger at 14-day threshold became central mechanism—Federal Council accepted it, AT1 rep demanded precise language, drove statement text negotiations through all rounds
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: Federal Council vs. CS CEO conflict over creditor haircuts discussed extensively (15-20% demand vs. 'creditors stay whole'), but ultimately resolved by automatic trigger framework—acknowledged but did not block decision
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 rep warned repeatedly that ambiguous language would invite Monday litigation, drove demand for precise trigger text, but did not force substantive change to rescue structure—noted as risk, not decision driver
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: 10 p.m. Friday UBS board deadline, 5:45 a.m. Sunday statement finalization, 6 a.m. announcement, 9:30 a.m. Monday market open—time pressure forced all key decisions and became binding constraint on negotiation cycles
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Wealth client and CS CEO repeatedly referenced Monday 9:30 panic risk and need for statement clarity, but this was context for decisions rather than forcing specific terms—background driver, not binding constraint
